prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional molecules that bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell removes the protein

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from phase separation (B049) to targeted protein degradation (B067) with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Reading the full first round, my case for B049 rested on its physical-chemical clarity, but I was the only member to prefer it, and even Linke, who ranked it first in the opening, now keeps it only as an alternative because the in-cell artefact question is unresolved. I have to take seriously that my field bias made me generous there. On the merits, degraders are also a physical-chemical story that I can evaluate on its own terms: a bifunctional molecule drives formation of a ternary complex, cooperativity and linker design are measurable thermodynamic quantities, and the ternary-complex structures (Ciulli) explain the selectivity rules. The principle is that removal by the cell replaces occupancy of a pocket, it was proposed by Crews and Deshaies in 2001, and it has been reproduced across many ligases, targets and laboratories. Six members ranked it and five placed it in the top three. My opening rank of eighth was about maturity and attribution, not about the science, and after the exchange I no longer think those two reservations outweigh the scale of the new capability.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is an approved drug, so clinical consequences are still prospective and the award could be seen as early. Attribution is the harder problem: the molecular-glue strand (Handa and Ito on cereblon; Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) has a different intellectual origin, and a three-name PROTAC citation leaves out people with serious claims. I would keep the citation strictly to bifunctional degraders and not claim the glue branch. Most of the field also relies on only a few E3 ligases (cereblon and VHL), so generality across the ubiquitin system is still partly asserted. B049 remains scientifically important, and if the committee finds the degrader credit unworkable I would return to it, provided the citation is limited to the demonstrated liquid-like demixing of multivalent biomolecules.

responses.point: Linke asked what claim I would put in a B049 citation that survives the artefact critique, and then moved B049 from first place to first alternative while placing B067 as the lead.
responses.response: My answer was a citation limited to liquid-like demixing as an organizing mechanism, with the criteria being reversible concentration thresholds and measured phase diagrams. I think that is defensible but narrow, and your own retreat shows that even the physicist who liked it most does not regard it as ready to lead. I accept that. I would also note that, as Lund colleagues, we should not count our moves as independent confirmation of each other, and my change to B067 rests on the arguments of Aili, Aqvist and Zou, not on yours.

responses.point: Aili asked whether my low opening rank for degraders was about the science or about attribution and maturity, and pointed to many clinical programmes and to the diffuse credit in B047 as well.
responses.response: It was attribution and maturity, not science. I accept the point on B047: the credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson and Langer is as diffuse as in B067, and the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification covers part of what makes lipid nanoparticles work, so I no longer rank it above degraders. The clinical programmes show that the chemistry transfers to real targets, and I agree that attribution is a reason to choose names carefully, not a reason to rank the discovery low. That is why I now support B067.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Crews and Deshaies but proposes Handa instead of Ciulli, arguing that the cereblon story links PROTACs and molecular glues into one achievement, while also noting that most of the field depends on only CRBN and VHL.
responses.response: I find the Handa argument serious, since cereblon is the ligase most used in the clinic. But I do not think the two strands are one achievement: Handa identified a target of thalidomide, which explains a drug, while the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work, is a design principle that any laboratory can reuse. A citation phrased around bifunctional design is accurate with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Using Handa would require a wider citation about hijacking the ubiquitin system, which the three-name limit cannot support without excluding Ito, Gray and Sakamoto. I would rather be precise and name the glue gap openly.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B013) for its maturity, routine use and clean Buchwald-Hartwig credit, with B067 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I agree that B013 is the safest option on maturity and attribution, and I said so in round one. The question I asked and which remains open is what in C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize, and your answer, that it needed its own ligand and mechanistic work, is fair but still describes an extension of the same disconnection logic. If you accept that maturity is the only thing keeping B067 from your first choice, I would ask whether widespread reproduction in many ligases and laboratories gives enough validation. I would not rank B013 above B067.

responses.point: Aqvist notes that if the glue and PROTAC strands are judged to be one achievement, his Crews-Deshaies-Ciulli trio is weaker than he has been treating it, and that the three-name limit forces an arguable cut.
responses.response: I share this concern and think the committee should decide it deliberately. My view is that the PROTAC concept stands as a separate achievement that does not depend on the glue branch, so a trio built on bifunctional molecules is internally complete even though it leaves out serious contributors. I would accept the cost of an honest narrow citation over a broad one that claims more than the three names have shown.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges PROTACs and molecular glues to be one achievement or two, which decides whether Ciulli or Handa should be the third name
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes recognition early in 2026, and I am not certain of the latest clinical status
Whether my change of preference reflects the scientific arguments or an overcorrection against my own field bias
Whether B049 can be given a citation narrow enough to survive the artefact critique, and whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag should be credited
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to any candidate on the shortlist. My research on lipid self-assembly and amyloid is scientifically close to B049 and B047, which is a field bias and not a recusal issue, and my move away from B049 reduces its influence on my position. I have no scientific overlap with B067. Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai are Lund colleagues, and Daniel Aili and Peter Brzezinski work in overlapping areas; none of these is a conflict with a candidate, and agreement between Lund members should not count as independent confirmation.
